rows.title: New payroll guidance for 2026
rows.excerpt: What changed, who it affects, and the two actions to take this month.
rows.body:
## What changed

PENCOM has published updated payroll guidance for the 2026 tax year. The headline numbers are small, the timing is not: two deductions change from the January payroll run.

### The two actions for this month

- Re-run your payroll template with the new PAYE bands before the 25th.
- Tell affected staff in writing before the first payslip lands.

If you use a payroll bureau, ask them to confirm in writing that the **2026 bands** are loaded. It is the most common failure we see in January.

Read the [full guidance](https://www.pencom.gov.ng/) before you file.

rows.title: The first ninety days decide the next three years
rows.excerpt: Onboarding is not an event. It is the clearest signal a new hire gets about what this place actually values.
rows.body:
## Why the first ninety days decide it

Most people decisions are made before a new hire has a laptop. The induction, the first manager conversation and the first piece of feedback set expectations that survive for years.

### What good looks like

- A named person, not a department, waiting on day one.
- A written 30/60/90 plan the new hire can argue with.
- One honest conversation at week two, not a survey at month three.

None of this needs budget. It needs someone to own it.
